cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-woven strip-cloth tobe/boubou gown with embroidered geometric neckline and pocket motifs, a classic West African men's robe style also worn by the Wolof; such garments are shared across neighboring Sahelian/West African peoples and cannot be distinguished by ethnicity alone.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Gown (tobe, boubou, riga): the body is composed of 102 uniform narrow strips of cotton, hand-spun and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips forming the body of the gown have been sewn vertically, while the sleeves are sewn horizontally. At the front is sewn a large pocket. The pocket, and back and front of the shoulder are hand-embroidered with the 'two knives' (aska biyu) pattern in satin stitch and button-hole eyelet stitch. The patterns are geometric in shape and  arrangement and can be found around the neck extending to a small spiral on  the back of the tunic. There is also triangular embroidery along the neck and on a small section of the front pocket which extends into a small spiral on the back of the neck. The sleeves and neck are hemmed. When assembled and embroidered, the entire gown has been dyed indigo, producing a uniform colour over the whole.
